messages:
ana: heads up — seeing a block of GPU nodes flip to NotReady in us-west2 after the kernel roll last night. Not the usual deviceplugin crashloop.
josh: same cluster? any kubelet logs? could be driver binary mismatch with the new kernel.
ana: yeah eu-west and us-west, but mostly us-west preemptible pool. kubelet shows node problem "driver checksum mismatch" and healthz failing.
node-monitor-bot: node/gpu-pool-3-7b7f status -> NotReady (Reason: DriverChecksumMismatch), affected pods evicted: 18
ria: oof. I haven't seen checksum mismatch before. grab dmesg and the driver version from one node?
ana: pasted quick logs:
```
[  123.456] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[  123.458] nvidia: driver version 515.76
kubelet: kubelet-healthz: FAILED: driver checksum 0x3a5f != expected 0x7b2c
```
sam: that expected checksum looks like image baked against the old kernel. The node image builder probably stamped an expected checksum into the device-plugin ConfigMap during image bake.
josh: cluster-autoscaler note: when nodes go NotReady during scale-up it can trigger rapid scale-outs and then scale-ins once nodes are cordoned. We saw budget spikes — cost hit for preemptible pool.
ana: exact. cost alert fired: preemptible-gpu spend +48% in 2h window.
ria: immediate mitigation: can we add a temporary taint to prevent workloads from scheduling to new GPU nodes until we fix? Or label them so autoscaler doesn't count them for GPU scheduling?
sam: we already have taint gpu: true:NoSchedule but autoscaler still considers capacity. We could tweak scaleDownUtilizationThreshold in autoscaler, but that's risky.
josh: quicker: patch device-plugin DaemonSet to add a startupProbe that waits on /var/run/nvidia/healthz and only registers plugin if health matches checksum. That prevents kubelet from seeing a half-broken plugin.
ana: nice. also rolling back kernel to last-known-good on the image might be fastest for clusters under heavy load.
deploy-bot: rolling-update started for node-image/gpu-preemptible:v2024-09-14 -> rollout paused (3/10 completed)
ria: can we add a fallback driver image to the hostpath plugin so if checksum mismatches it uses prebuilt bin in /opt/nvidia/legacy? avoids full image rollback.
sam: yes, implement fallback in device-plugin: if checksum mismatch, log and attempt fallback binary, set healthz=ok. Need careful testing.
ana: for now, I've cordoned the problematic nodes and set node annotations to block autoscaler scale-down: kubectl annotate node/gpu-pool-* autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true
josh: also propose adding an alert: driver-healthz mismatch >5 nodes -> runbook page and automatic pause of preemptible scaling.
ria: runbook snippet (copy):
```
1) cordon affected nodes: kubectl cordon <node>
2) check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log for checksum tag
3) if mismatch, flip to fallback driver: sudo cp /opt/nvidia/legacy/libnvidia.so /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/updates
4) restart nvidia-hostengine and kubelet
```
ana: assigning follow-ups: @josh take autoscaler tuning; @sam and @ria prototype fallback in device-plugin; I'll coordinate rollback window with release infra.
josh: ack — will open a CR and add alert rule.
sam: will start a small canary job in staging testing fallback binary.
node-monitor-bot: Alert created: DRV-CHECKSUM-001 (severity=high) — notification sent to #oncall
ana: thanks. next 30m we'll watch cost and node churn, I'll update this thread with any progress.
